title: Affine chart and graph presentation for prescribed differential coordinates
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $U$ a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $u\in U$, $d\geq0$ and $h_1,\ldots,h_d\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Suppose their differentials form a $\kappa(u)$-basis of $\Omega_{U/k,u}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{U,u}}\kappa(u)$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-pc-module-stalk-functor, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-module-base-change], where a basis is a linearly independent spanning family. There exist an affine open neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$ of $u$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], integers $n\geq r\geq0$ with $n=r+d$, and a standard smooth $k$-algebra presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] $$\alpha:k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_r)\xrightarrow{\sim}A.$$ Write $a_b=\alpha(\overline y_b)$ and let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ correspond to $u$. There is a canonical identification $K=\kappa(u)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and a $K$-linear isomorphism $$\Phi:\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{U/k,u}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{U,u}}K,\qquad \omega\otimes\lambda\longmapsto\operatorname{germ}_u(\omega)\otimes\lambda,$$ with $\Omega_{A/k}$ the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. It carries $d(h_j|_W)\otimes1$ to the specified differential class, and $da_{r+1}\otimes1,\ldots,da_n\otimes1$ is a $K$-basis of its source. There are polynomials $H_j\in k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]$ mapping to $h_j|_W$. Put $R=k[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and give $A$ its $R$-algebra structure by $T_j\mapsto h_j|_W$. The map $y_b\mapsto a_b$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $$R[y_1,\ldots,y_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_r,H_1-T_1,\ldots,H_d-T_d)\xrightarrow{\sim}A.$$ Under $\operatorname{Spec}R=\mathbf A^d_k$ [def-sbc-affine-space], this $R$-algebra structure gives the restriction to $W$ of the $k$-morphism with coordinate functions $h_j$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-locally-standard-smooth] to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $u$. The affine target neighbourhood contains the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so is the whole target. Thus obtain an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $u$, with $A$ standard smooth over $k$. Unpack [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] to choose $n\ge r\ge0$, the polynomials $F_i$, and the isomorphism $\alpha$ of the statement. Set $a_b=\alpha(\overline y_b)$ and let $\mathfrak q$ be the point corresponding to $u$. No equality $n-r=d$ has yet been assumed.

By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}$ through the germ map. Quotient by their corresponding maximal ideals to identify $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ with $K=\kappa(u)$. Put $M=\Omega_{A/k}$. The affine description in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] identifies $\Omega_{U/k}|_W$ with $\widetilde M$, respecting derivations. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] its stalk is $M_{\mathfrak q}$, and the germ of $\omega$ corresponds to $\omega/1$. These identifications apply to this particular standard smooth chart; they do not require choosing a different affine neighbourhood.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis], $M$ has $A$-basis $da_{r+1},\ldots,da_n$. Their tensors with $1$ are a $K$-basis: tensor the basis coordinate maps with $K$; their coefficient functions and the finite-sum reconstruction remain inverse, by [def-weil-module-base-change]. Step 3 and the hypothesis give another basis of this same space of length $d$. The two basis coordinate isomorphisms therefore give $K^{n-r}\cong K^d$. Since $K$ is a field, it is nontrivial, and [lem-sfb-commutative-ring-invariant-basis-number] gives $n-r=d$, hence $n=r+d$. This proves both the required size and the asserted basis in the source of $\Phi$.

source.place: Tag 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth), part (2); finite basis comparison after extension to the residue field

proof.text: The quotient map $k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]\to A$ is surjective, so choose lifts $H_j$ of $h_j|_W$. Let $R=k[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ act on $A$ by evaluation $T_j\mapsto h_j|_W$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $B=R[y_1,\ldots,y_n]/(F_i,H_j-T_j)$. Evaluation $y_b\mapsto a_b$ kills every displayed relation, and so gives an $R$-algebra map $\beta:B\to A$. In the other direction the classes of $y_b$ in $B$ annihilate all $F_i$, hence define $k[y]/(F_i)\to B$. Composing with $\alpha^{-1}$ gives $\gamma:A\to B$. It is $R$-linear because $\gamma(h_j|_W)=H_j(\overline y)=\overline T_j$. Now $\beta\gamma$ is the identity on all the $a_b$, which generate $A$ over $k$; $\gamma\beta$ fixes all $\overline y_b$ and $\overline T_j$, which generate $B$ over $k$. The polynomial universal property makes both composites identities, proving the asserted graph isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-global-sections], the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ defined by this algebra structure pulls back $T_j$ to $h_j|_W$. With $\operatorname{Spec}R=\mathbf A^d_k$, these are exactly the coordinate pullbacks of the restriction of the specified $k$-morphism on $U$. Polynomial maps agreeing on the $T_j$ agree by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and their affine scheme morphisms agree by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. This proves the last clause.
